preconditions.description: The number of cities n is an integer between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= p_i < i for i in range(2, n + 1))
preconditions.description: The parent array p defines a valid tree structure where each city i (2 ≤ i ≤ n) is connected to city p_i (1 ≤ p_i < i) by a road.
The number of bus routes m is an integer between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for (a, b) in bus_routes)
preconditions.description: Each bus route is a pair of distinct cities (a, b) where 1 ≤ a, b ≤ n.
The number of queries q is an integer between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n and 1 <= u <= n and v != u for (v, u) in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query is a pair of distinct cities (v, u) where 1 ≤ v, u ≤ n.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all((v, u) in queries and (v != u) and (1 <= answer <= q) for (v, u), answer in zip(queries, [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()]))
postconditions.description: For each query (v, u), the output line is an integer answer representing the minimum number of buses needed to travel from v to u, or -1 if no such path exists.

postconditions.expression: all((answer == -1) or (answer >= 1) for answer in [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()])
postconditions.description: If a path exists, the answer is a positive integer representing the minimum number of buses; otherwise, it is -1.

postconditions.expression: all((answer == -1) or (any((a == v or b == v) and (a == u or b == u) for (a, b) in bus_routes)) or (any((a == v or b == v) and (a == u or b == u) for (a, b) in bus_routes) for _ in range(1, answer)) for (v, u), answer in zip(queries, [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()]))
postconditions.description: If the answer is not -1, there exists a sequence of bus routes (possibly with intermediate stops) that allows travel from v to u using exactly 'answer' buses. The sequence respects the shortest path constraint of each bus route (i.e., buses only travel along the shortest path between their endpoints in the tree).
